Summary: Fully Connected Networks vs CNNs
Can learn translation invariance by learning
similar feature detectors at many spatial
locations (when given lots of training data)
CNNs avoid learning redundancy by introducing architectural
inductive biases—shared weights tied to local receptive fields enable
reusable feature detectors while spatial pooling builds invariance

1. Propagate training data through network to predict output
2. Measure error of predictions using a loss function
3. Calculate gradients of the loss function to determine how
each model parameter contributed to the error; weight
sharing accounted for by summing partial derivative values
for all connections that share the same parameter
4. Update each parameter using calculated gradients
1. Propagate training data through network to predict output
2. Measure error of predictions using a loss function
3. Calculate gradients of the loss function to determine how
each model parameter contributed to the error; weight
sharing accounted for by summing partial derivative values
for all connections that share the same parameter
4. Update each parameter using calculated gradients
• Approach: only inputs that contribute to an output are blamed and so receive
gradients for parameter updating; all other paths get 0 gradient
• e.g., max pooling: gradient flows only to the input that was the max with other paths getting
0 gradient; since no learning happens, the gradient just passes through to the earlier layer
